evidence: Sec 3.1.2: the Human-AI Selection Module chooses among AI alone or AI plus a number of annotators, and "the cost in Equation (5) represents the cost of one unit per expert's annotation".
method: LECOMH: selection module picks AI alone or AI plus k human annotators per image (Gumbel-softmax, per-annotation cost); collaboration MLP fuses predictions; trained from noisy multi-rater labels without clean labels.
evaluation: CIFAR-10N/10H, synthetic IDN20/50, Chaoyang, NIH chest X-ray; vs 6 single-expert L2D, Multi_L2D, CET, multi-rater methods; accuracy at 50% coverage 94.19-99.58, best on all six; RTX A6000; no inference latency.
contribution: Learns, from noisy multi-rater labels alone, when a classifier should decide by itself and when to consult one or more human experts and fuse their labels, beating learning-to-defer baselines on image and medical benchmarks.
flag: (iii) and (i) apply: choice among AI alone and several human experts, with real radiologist, pathologist and crowd labels at test time. Check: this is learning to complement (fusing AI and human labels), not a pure hand-off, and annotators are picked at random so there is no per-expert routing; one-shot image classification, accuracy-coverage only, no safety or intervention metric; the humans are stored labels, not a studied takeover, so e and the human handoff cell were not claimed. Table 1 and Table 2 baseline values appear inconsistent in the arXiv version (e.g. RS on CIFAR-10H 96.65 vs 98.14) and LECOMH figures differ slightly between Tables 1, 2 and 5; verify against the journal version. Cost trade-off shown in a figure only.

title: A safety-oriented multimodal decision framework for venipuncture assistance
evidence: "V4 removes the abstention mechanism by forcing all Avoid and Retake outputs back to Recommend" (Sec 4.6)
method: Vein-SmartSite: UNet++ vein segmentation, scored candidate puncture points, frozen Qwen-VL-Max contraindication gate, and a min-of-three-confidences threshold that outputs Recommend, Avoid or Retake to the nurse.
evaluation: 523 NIR images; 518/511 nurse-consensus cases: sensitivity 71.93%, specificity 71.15%, conditional unsafe-recommendation 14.71%, overall 0.98%; ablation n=37; abstain 21.62%; 9-11 s per case, about USD 700 hardware, server-side inference.
contribution: A low-cost venipuncture assistant that withholds a puncture-site recommendation and asks the nurse to re-image or change site when segmentation, geometry or vision-language confidence is low.
flag: BORDERLINE, closest to (i)/(iv): a gate that withholds a recommendation and hands back to a nurse in a clinical task. Recommended exclude because it is a one-shot, per-image reject option applied to a domain, advisory only ("The decision remains with the operator"), and abstention is one of four pipeline components rather than the sole contribution. Evidence for the abstention mechanism itself is thin: the ablation (Table 4) rests on only two contraindication-positive cases, so unsafe rate 100% (no abstention) vs 50% (full) is a one-case difference, and the authors say so; the 14.71% figure is 5 of 34 cases with CI 3.45-27.78. Abstention costs Top-3 hit 59.46% -> 45.95%. Abstract says Top-3 65.79% on n=38 but ablation uses n=37. Threshold tau=0.320 from a fixed 20% abstention budget, not swept. Safety cohort overlaps training images and labels were not collected blind. PPV 23.56% (133 of 174 warnings disagreed with nurses). Nurses rated abstained cases (Likert mean 3.03) and a timing study shows 10.8-20.5% faster site selection, which is why (e) is listed, but takeover itself is not measured. Latency 9-11 s uses a hosted MLLM endpoint, not edge. Record year 2027 is the volume date (Pattern Recognition 183); supplementary tables not in the text file.

title: Probabilistic personalised cascade with abstention
evidence: "decide whether to return a label at the current stage of the cascade, or to pay for a new feature acquisition" (Sec 2)
method: Cascade as a POMDP trained by deep Q-learning: a Gaussian graphical-model classifier shares parameters with a neural rejector that, at each stage, either classifies or abstains and buys another feature.
evaluation: 2 simulated and 3 UCI medical datasets (Heart, Mammographic, Breast), 10-fold CV; baselines Clertant et al. 2019 and Janisch et al. 2019; accuracy vs number of acquired features and training time, figures only.
contribution: A cost-sensitive cascade whose rejector repeatedly abstains to acquire another feature before classifying, reaching accuracy comparable to deep Q-network cascades with markedly shorter training time.
flag: BORDERLINE, (ii) arguably applies: abstain-or-classify is an action taken over stages in a POMDP. Recommended exclude because the abstention is a cost-driven decision to acquire the next feature (classification with costly features), there is no hand-off, safeguard or safety outcome, and the paper's stated novelty is the unified probabilistic classifier, missing-value handling and training speed, not the deferral rule (the rejector is taken from Clertant et al. with a changed first-layer activation). If the maintainer reads (ii) broadly this could be an include; exclude-E4 is the alternative code. No numeric results anywhere in the text: all results are plots (Figs 3-16), and the 'up to 5 times faster' claim in the contributions is supported only by the learning-time figures. Authors concede accuracy is only comparable and can be worse than baselines when the Gaussian assumption fails. Convex-hull model selection is done on the TEST set (Sec 6). Hardware not stated. Supplementary material not in the file.

title: Estimating the accuracy of selective classifiers without labels using Venn-Abers predictors
evidence: "we leverage the calibration properties of Venn-Abers predictors to estimate the accuracy on the non-rejected samples at inference time" (Summary)
method: Selective classifier built on inductive Venn-Abers calibration; averages the lower/upper confidences over accepted samples to estimate selective accuracy without labels, plus a Poisson-binomial lower bound for worst-case accuracy.
evaluation: 24 binary tabular datasets, tree/forest/XGBoost, 500 hold-out repetitions, rejection 10-90%; baselines uncalibrated, isotonic, Platt, conformal reject option; decision-tree mean abs error 0.003 (AvgVA) vs 0.007 CRO, 0.039 uncalibrated.
contribution: Uses Venn-Abers predictors to estimate, without labels, the accuracy a selective classifier will achieve on the cases it accepts, with a guaranteed interval and a worst-case lower bound.
flag: Closest to (v) but recommended exclude: one-shot selective classification on tabular benchmarks, and the contribution is label-free ESTIMATION of selective accuracy, not the abstain/defer rule (rejection is a plain confidence ranking at a user-set rate). Proved: Propositions 1-4 and Corollaries 1-3 - the Venn-Abers interval contains a perfectly calibrated confidence for correctness, so averaged bounds bracket selective accuracy and a Poisson-binomial inversion gives a 1-delta lower bound; experiments accompany. If the maintainer counts accuracy guarantees for selective classifiers as (v) 'bounds', this becomes an include. Caveat the authors state themselves: the guarantees hold only for the interval/unknown selector, and the practical single-valued estimators (AvgVA, RegVA) that produce the headline results lose them; RegVA did not beat uncalibrated random forest. i.i.d. assumption, no distribution shift tested, tree models only, binary only. Human review is motivation only, no human study. Declares ChatGPT use for language editing. Record year 2026; issue date is 8 January 2027, 'in press' proof. Tables 3-7 and the Discussion read in part; supplement not in file.

title: Systems-theoretic interdependence analysis in robot-assisted warehouse management
evidence: "When warehouse robots experience momentarily navigation loss or network connection issues, bots will stop navigating for safety reasons, and produce a visual signal to indicate that the robot needs assistance from a human operator to perform a reset procedure." (Section 5.2, Case study highlight #2)
method: Functional Resonance Analysis Method combined with Interdependence Analysis (Observability, Predictability, Directability) as a five-step qualitative framework modelling human-robot co-agency and inter-agent dependencies in an AMR-assisted warehouse.
evaluation: No quantitative evaluation: 13 open-ended interviews (6 operators, 5 supervisors-managers, 2 managers; 9 h) plus 8 h naturalistic observation, qualitative OPD dependency tables and one incident instantiation; no safety metric, no baseline, no ablation.
contribution: A combined FRAM and Interdependence Analysis framework that maps observability, predictability and directability between human operators, supervisors and warehouse robots to expose emergent hazards and work-system dependencies in robot-assisted warehousing.
flag: learned or AI system guarded: no - LIDAR and QR-code navigating warehouse AMRs under a rule-based robot control system. (e) holds as subject matter (operator and supervisor observability-predictability-directability over the robots, operator reset when a robot halts and defers), but the paper is a qualitative case description and fails the evaluation floor: the authors themselves write 'The contribution of this paper is restricted to a case description'. The 0-0.5-1 phenotype values in the RAM tables are analyst codings, not measurements; the stair-fall incident is a single anecdote and no human-robot collision was ever reported by informants, so the one safety claim rests on absence of reported events; most observation was replaced by online webcam walkarounds and online interviews because of COVID access restrictions. Tables 3 and 4, which carry the OPD results, are images and unreadable in the extracted text. Borderline E3 as a method-application case study.

title: 21 Optimizing AI-physician collaboration for enhanced diagnostic accuracy: A case study on acute respiratory distress syndrome detection using chest X-ray imaging
venue: Journal of Clinical and Translational Science
evidence: "2) physician-aided AI: the AI model interprets chest X-rays first and defers to a physician if uncertain" (METHODS/STUDY POPULATION)
method: Compares three AI-physician collaboration strategies for ARDS detection on chest X-rays: physician defers to AI when uncertain, AI defers to physician when uncertain, and averaging both interpretations.
evaluation: 414 chest X-rays from 115 patients, six physician reads each; accuracy: AI 84.7%, physicians 80.8%, AI-aided physician 82.4%, physician-aided AI 86.9%, averaging 86%; up to 79% reads off-loaded. No hardware or latency.
contribution: Retrospective ARDS chest X-ray study showing that an AI model deferring uncertain cases to physicians reaches 86.9% accuracy, above AI alone (84.7%) or physicians alone (80.8%), while off-loading up to 79% of reads.
flag: (i) deferral to a human expert, uncertainty-triggered and in both directions. BORDERLINE: the text is a one-paragraph conference abstract (JCTS 2025 Abstract Supplement, abstract no. 21, pages 7-8 of a multi-abstract file; located by title, not a wrong file). No detail on the deferral rule, uncertainty measure, thresholds, data split or statistics; no confidence intervals; single site, 115 patients. The evaluation floor is met only on the stated accuracies. Maintainer may prefer exclude-E2 for an abstract-only record, or substitute the authors' full journal article on the same study if one exists (I believe one was published around 2023 but did not verify; no web access used).

title: Enhancing the reliability and accuracy of AI-enabled diagnosis via complementarity-driven deferral to clinicians
evidence: "For a given medical image, the deferral AI takes as input the confidence score from the predictive AI and decides to either use the predictive AI model or defer, in which case the medical image is evaluated using a standard clinical workflow." (Introduction)
method: CoDoC: a learned deferral function over a locked black-box model's confidence score; defers to the clinical workflow where an estimated advantage function favours clinicians (optimal rule derived in Proposition 1).
evaluation: Retrospective UK/US mammography and TB chest X-ray data vs AI-only, clinician-only and threshold-search baselines; sensitivity, specificity, reads per case with CIs. No hardware or latency reported.
contribution: CoDoC learns when a locked diagnostic model should defer to clinicians, improving specificity or sensitivity over AI-only and double-reading baselines in breast cancer and TB screening while cutting human reads.
flag: (i) deferral to human clinicians, with (v)-style derivation of the optimal deferral rule from P(z,h|y). One-shot per case, not sequential. Body figures read: vs standalone AI specificity +1.6% or sensitivity +7.7% (single-reader deferral, 0.23-0.34 extra reads per case); vs UK double reading sensitivity +3.4% or specificity +0.8% with 1.4 fewer reads per case; TB 5-15% false-positive reduction for 3 of 5 commercial systems. The abstract's 66% workload reduction I could not locate as a literal figure in the body text (likely tables or supplement); the 25% appears in the body as recall-to-assessment rate 127 to 96 per 1,000. All evaluation is retrospective with independent reads; authors state prospective validation is still needed. Tables, supplement and second half of Methods were skimmed by keyword, not read line by line.

title: A benchmarking framework and dataset for learning to defer in human-AI decision-making
evidence: "Finally we observe that both OvA and DeCCaF obtain significantly better results than all non-L2D baselines, with the methods achieving an average 11% and 15% decrease, respectively, in the misclassification cost over the Random Assignment baseline." (Technical Validation, Deferral Results)
method: OpenL2D: framework generating synthetic experts with feature-dependent error, bias and work-capacity constraints; yields the FiFAR fraud alert-review dataset (50 synthetic analysts, 30K instances) and benchmarks multi-expert L2D methods.
evaluation: Bank account fraud alerts; OvA and DeCCaF vs full rejection, classifier-only and random deferral over 5 teams of 10 experts under capacity constraints; misclassification cost with 95% CI, expert-model AUC and ECE. No latency.
contribution: OpenL2D and the FiFAR dataset provide a capacity-constrained multi-expert learning-to-defer benchmark for fraud review, in which two L2D methods cut misclassification cost 11-15% over random assignment and rankings change with team composition.
flag: (iii) deferral among multiple experts, also (i). CAUTION: this is a Scientific Data descriptor; the contribution is a benchmark and dataset, not a new deferral mechanism, and the experts are SYNTHETIC (simulated analysts validated against literature and one private real-analyst dataset), so criterion (e) is not credited and human handoff is simulated only. Deferral rate is fixed at 10/11 by design and assignment is batch-wise under capacity constraints, not a safety halt. Only two L2D methods benchmarked, both from the same group's line of work (Feedzai). Expert-correctness AUC does not exceed 0.65. Maintainer should decide whether a benchmark paper counts as main-contribution deferral; if not, exclude-E1. Read: summary, methods overview, testing setup, technical validation (deferral results), limitations; data-record field listings skipped.

title: Conformal selective prediction with cost aware deferral for safe clinical triage under distribution shift
evidence: "Deferral follows a certainty-threshold rule on the calibrated posterior, where a case is routed to human review if the maximum predicted class probability falls below a threshold" (Deferral policy and cost matrix)
method: Temperature-scaled MLP for 6-hour early sepsis prediction with split, Mondrian and weighted conformal sets; a single max-probability threshold, chosen to minimise an asymmetric expected cost, defers cases to clinicians.
evaluation: PhysioNet 2019, 2,155 patients, temporal ID/OOD test splits; retained-case error -49.6% ID and -46.7% OOD at 80% coverage; expected cost 0.5640/0.7053; ECE 0.016/0.030; baseline is predict-all or always-negative. No latency.
contribution: Combines calibrated probabilities, conformal prediction sets and a cost-optimised confidence threshold to defer uncertain early-sepsis predictions to clinicians, reporting risk-coverage gains under temporal shift on PhysioNet 2019.
flag: none of (i)-(v) in substance: nominally (i) deferral to clinicians, but no clinician is modelled or measured; deferral is a fixed max-probability threshold with a flat deferral cost of 2, i.e. one-shot selective classification applied to a domain and judged by risk-coverage. Not sequential despite time-series source data (one feature vector per patient). Weak evidence: only 2,155 patients (ID test 344, about 20 positives), base AUROC 0.698 ID; the paper itself states the optimised operating point is slightly WORSE than the trivial always-negative baseline on the ID split under the original costs; gains of 18.5-30% appear only under alternative cost ratios. No comparison against other selective-prediction or L2D methods. Conformal sets are not actually used by the deferral rule that is evaluated.

title: Selective multipathology chest X-ray classification via rejection mechanisms
evidence: "it is rejected only if all predicted classes are deemed uncertain." (Sec 3.4); abstract: "improving reliability by deferring ambiguous cases to clinical experts."
method: DenseNet-121 four-pathology chest X-ray classifier with post-hoc entropy-based or confidence-interval-based rejection; quantile-calibrated thresholds, image rejected only when every class is uncertain.
evaluation: PadChest, NIH, MIMIC-CXR; baseline is the same model without rejection; AUC, F1, rejection rate. Mean AUC stated 0.79 (none), 0.81 (interval), 0.83 (entropy). No hardware/latency.
contribution: Adds entropy- and interval-based rejection to a multi-label chest X-ray classifier and reports modest AUC changes on retained cases across three datasets at rejection rates from about 1% to 46%.
flag: none of (i)-(v): a one-shot classifier with a reject option applied to a domain. Deferral to clinicians is asserted but never evaluated (no reader study, no expert accuracy on deferred cases), so (i) and criterion e do not hold. arXiv title differs slightly from the record ("Multi-Pathology Chest X-Ray Classification with Rejection Mechanisms") but it is the same work; journal version may differ. Doubts: stated mean AUCs 0.79/0.81/0.83 do not match the per-class Table 3 values, which average about 0.79/0.79/0.80; rejection lowers AUC in several cells (NIH Consolidation 73.3 to 68.04 at 43% rejected; Consolidation 0.87 to 0.77 in Table 3); rejection cap stated as 10% in Sec 3.4 and 25% in Sec 3.5; no risk-coverage curves; no comparison with other uncertainty methods.

title: Population-scale cross-sectional observational study for AI-powered TB screening on one million CXRs
evidence: "By selectively deferring only cases with findings to radiologists, the model has the potential to automate up to 80% of routine CXR reporting." (Abstract)
method: AIRIS-TB: chest X-ray classifier (no-finding vs suspicious) used as a first screen; scans scored below a threshold are auto-reported, the rest are routed to radiologists.
evaluation: Quasi-prospective evaluation on about 1.04M CXRs (Abu Dhabi, 2022-2024) plus external sets; AUC 98.51%, FNR 1.57% vs radiologists 1.85%, TB-FNR 0%, workload reduction 40% (safe) or 80% (optimal). No latency.
contribution: Population-scale validation of a TB screening classifier that auto-reports no-finding chest X-rays and routes suspicious ones to radiologists, reporting 1.57% false negatives and up to 80% workload reduction on one million scans.
flag: none of (i)-(v): the paper is a diagnostic-accuracy validation of a classifier; the so-called deferral is simply the positive (suspicious) class being sent on for radiologist review at a fixed score threshold, not an abstain or defer decision based on model uncertainty or relative human-AI competence, and no deferral rule is proposed or compared. Workload figures are projected (the model was not actually deployed to auto-report; radiologists read all scans), and reference labels come from those same radiologists, with some labels corrected after review to reach 0% TB-FNR. Source text has ligature characters; the quote was normalised to ASCII (findings). Supplementary sections not available in the text.

title: From confidence to caution: conformal gating for cross-session motor imagery brain–computer interfaces
evidence: "This protocol is an offline simulation of deployment-time command gating, not an online closed-loop BCI evaluation." (Sec. 3.5)
method: Post-hoc command gate on a DeepConvNet motor-imagery EEG classifier: conformal sets (THR, RAPS, RAPS-Opt) issue a command only for singleton sets, else abstain; compared with Chow confidence-threshold rejection.
evaluation: Offline, OpenBMI (54 subj, 2-class) and BCIC IV-2a (9 subj, 4-class), 5 chronological splits; ungated wrong-decisive 37.5%/35.5% vs gated 9-16%/6-8%; decision rate, coverage, F0.5, utility U(lambda). No latency or hardware.
contribution: Offline comparison of conformal and Chow gating for cross-session motor-imagery BCI commands, showing conformal gates cut wrong-decisive commands from about 36% to 6-16% at the cost of abstaining on roughly half of trials.
flag: none of (i)-(v) cleanly; (iv) is arguable: the gate withholds a device command and the paper frames this as safety, but it is one-shot per-trial selective classification applied to a domain, evaluated offline on healthy-subject public datasets with no device, no closed loop, no latency and no human or fallback takeover. No new method or theory (existing THR/RAPS/Chow compared). If the maintainer reads (iv) broadly this could be include: abstention is the main contribution and baselines (ungated, Chow) are quantitative. Abstract numbers match Table 4 and the conclusion. Appendices (alpha sweep, backbone ablation) skimmed only.

title: Clinicians need to review only half of LLM outputs to preserve diagnostic accuracy: the SCOUT randomised crossover trial
evidence: "High-uncertainty cases are deferred to clinicians; low-uncertainty cases are accepted automatically." (Methods)
method: SCOUT: model-agnostic meta-verification that triangulates auxiliary-model disagreement, repeated-inference inconsistency and a reasoning-critique checker to defer unreliable LLM diagnostic outputs to clinicians and auto-accept the rest.
evaluation: CHD subtyping on MIMIC-IV (n=1866), prospective cohort (n=110), vessel counting (n=286): 17.8-54.5% reviewed, final accuracy 99.1-100%. Crossover trial, 7 clinicians vs full manual review: time -59.3% (0.37 vs 0.92 min), accuracy 90.8% vs 89.4%.
contribution: Uncertainty-triangulation gate that defers only unreliable LLM cardiology outputs to clinicians; in a seven-reader randomised crossover trial it cut review time by 59% with diagnostic accuracy comparable to full manual review.
flag: (i) deferral to human experts, with the handoff itself trialled. CONFERENCE ABSTRACT ONLY (Eur Heart J supplement, about 300 words; figures not in text): no detail on thresholds, the LLM used, or any comparison of the deferral rule against a simpler uncertainty baseline; the only comparator is review-everything. Validation 'final accuracies 99.1-100%' sit oddly beside 90.8% accuracy in the trial (probably assumes perfect human review in validation; not explained). Title says 'half', body says 17.8-54.5%. Only 7 readers, P=0.016. Single-case one-shot deferral, not sequential. Maintainer may judge an abstract too thin for extraction (E2). The text file also contains a second, unrelated abstract (LLM heart failure therapy) after this one; ignored.

title: Fast classification rates without standard margin assumptions
evidence: "fast classification rates are possible without any additional assumptions" once the learner may abstain at cost slightly below one half (Sec 1.3); Thm 2.1 gives the bound in Chow's reject model.
method: Agnostic VC-class learning in Chow's reject-option model: abstain where almost-ERMs disagree, select by empirical reject risk; then use this to get fast rates for non-abstaining classifiers.
evaluation: Theory only, no experiments. Proved: excess risk of order (d log(n/d)+log(1/delta))/(np) with reject cost 1/2-p, no margin assumption (Thm 2.1); Massart-type rate in misspecified case (Thm 3.2).
contribution: Proves that allowing a classifier to abstain at cost just under one half yields fast O(d log n/n) agnostic rates for VC classes with no margin assumption.
flag: (v), borderline: Thm 2.1 is a foundational reject-option bound and the first headline result, but the paper frames abstention as a device for fast rates and Sec 3 turns it back into ordinary classifiers; maintainer may judge abstention is not the MAIN contribution and prefer exclude-E1. Pure theory, no experiments, no runtime mechanism evaluated. Record is the journal version; arXiv preprint read.

title: GoGet: A multi-model multimodal assistive agent with Disagreement-Gated Grounding
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Advanced Algorithms and Neural Networks, AANN 2026
evidence: "It is a selective-prediction policy over the composed output." (Sec. I)
method: DAGF: in a four-model local assistive agent, a visual count from the segmenter is asserted only when the VLM count agrees within tolerance; otherwise the agent abstains with a hedged estimate. DAGF-R adds a segmenter-confidence floor.
evaluation: 43 synthetic scenes, 260 COCO images, MuJoCo robot (10 scenes). COCO confident-error 0.63 to 0.25 at 0.57 coverage (p<0.001) vs naive grounding; DAGF-R 0.26 to 0.14; AURC 0.13 vs 0.17 random. RTX 5090; grounded turn 4.75 s median.
contribution: Cross-model disagreement between a segmenter and a vision-language model used as an abstention signal for visual counting in a local multimodal agent, halving confidently wrong counts on COCO images at 57% coverage.
flag: none of (i)-(v): one-shot selective prediction on single counting questions; abstention returns a hedged answer, with no handoff to a human or safeguard and no safety action gated. Weak hook for (ii): in a simulated robot the abstention cues an approach-and-recount, but only 10 MuJoCo scenes and the closed loop reaches 0.40-0.70 vs 1.00 for always approaching, so abstention-driven active perception is not shown to help. On synthetic scenes DAGF lowers exact-match (0.79 vs 0.91). Abstract numbers match Table I. Router macro-F1 1.00 is on a lexically separable set by the authors' own admission. Short conference paper (AANN).

title: A Time-Aware Approach for MOOC Dropout Prediction Based on Rule Induction and Sequential Three-Way Decisions
evidence: "If the prediction is BND then uncertainty has been recognized and the classification process continues to the next iteration where information gathered during a new timeslot has been acquired." (Sec. VI-A)
method: Sequential three-way decisions with probabilistic rough sets plus CN2 rule induction: at the end of each weekly timeslot a rule classifier labels a student dropout, non-dropout, or boundary, deferring boundary cases to the next week.
evaluation: KDD Cup 2015 XuetangX, 40k balanced rows, 6 timeslots; first-week precision 0.861, recall 0.853, AUC 0.875 vs published MFCN-VIB 10-day 0.832/0.937/0.798; whole pipeline accuracy 0.76, F1 0.77, AUC 0.87. No latency.
contribution: Week-by-week MOOC dropout predictor that uses sequential three-way decisions to classify students when evidence suffices and defer uncertain cases to the next week, built from human-readable CN2 rules.
flag: (ii) deferral over time is the stated main contribution, but the evaluation is weak and borderline exclude-E2: there is NO ablation against a non-deferring classifier and no reported deferral rate or time-to-decision in the extracted text (Tables 1-4 are images, values missing from the text file; check the PDF). Baselines are numbers copied from other papers under different protocols (cross-validation vs 80/20, 10 days vs 7 days). Per-iteration scores appear to be measured against the rough-set tri-partition labels (POS/BND/NEG), not true dropout, which is partly circular; the honest end-to-end figure (accuracy 0.76, F1 0.77) is below the cited SVM baseline (0.85, 0.91) and the authors call it a 'worst case'. Thresholds 'empirically fixed'. Not safety-critical; no human handoff studied (staff intervention only mentioned). Deferral cost and irreversibility (student lost while waiting) not modelled.

title: From Defect Prediction to Defect Triage: Evaluating Accepted Risk and Review Effort With CReST-DP
evidence: "CReST-DP should be read as a decision-layer evaluation framework, not as a new abstention principle." (Sec. VI-A)
method: CReST-DP: an accept-or-route layer over a validation-selected defect predictor; the Inspection policy routes artifacts for additional review using probability, threshold-distance, effort and OOD signals; evaluated by accepted error, AFNE, coverage, routed effort.
evaluation: 18 static defect datasets x 5 seeds x 5 folds (450 settings), offline; at 70.13% coverage Inspection AE 0.0842, AFNE 0.2444 vs matched random 0.1359, 0.3708; single-signal reject rules as baselines; routed-effort 0.3385. No latency.
contribution: Decision-layer evaluation framework for software defect prediction that reports accepted error, missed-defect exposure and routed review effort for accept-or-route policies at matched coverage across 18 datasets.
flag: none of (i)-(v): one-shot reject option applied to a domain; the authors themselves disclaim a new reject-option principle. Routing is nominally to human review, but it is entirely offline and retrospective - no reviewers, no measured review time, no pilot (stated in limitations) - so (i) and criterion (e) are not met. Inspection is not the best rule: single-signal rules get lower AE or AFNE at more routed effort. Track B (ApacheJIT) is exploratory and cannot be reproduced from preserved artifacts by the authors' own account. Abstract numbers match Sec. VI. Read abstract, intro, related work, problem formulation, results summary, discussion and limitations; skimmed protocol detail and sensitivity tables (several tables are images, absent from the text).

title: No Representation Consistently Beats the Simple Baseline: A Pre-Registered Audit of Uncertainty Representations and Threshold Tuning for Edge Data-Quality Governance
evidence: "We call this task edge data-quality governance: for each incoming value the device decides whether to accept, clean, anonymize, compress, reject, or escalate (send-to-cloud) it." (Sec. I)
method: Pre-registered audit: nine uncertainty representations derived from one MC-Dropout stack feed a fixed five-threshold accept-or-escalate engine; ten threshold tuners compared at equal budget; conformal risk control on the escalation threshold.
evaluation: Synthetic benchmark plus four real defect-labeled tables; max-softmax AUGRC 0.930 vs neutrosophic 0.974; tuned cost 3.81 to 0.85 equals escalate-all; x86 CPU inference under 1 ms.
contribution: A pre-registered audit finds no fuzzy or neutrosophic uncertainty representation consistently beats max-softmax for accept-or-escalate data-quality decisions, and tuned thresholds collapse to escalating nearly everything.
flag: none of (i)-(v): one-shot per-cell selective prediction with uncertainty scores judged by risk-coverage area (AUGRC); the escalate target is a cloud service, not a human or safeguard, and is never modelled. Negative-result audit, not a new mechanism. Tuned policies escalate 0.89-0.99 of cells, so the deferral rule is degenerate on real data. Edge claim rests on an x86 single-thread profile only (Table 26), no edge hardware. Six-action policy validated on synthetic data only. Authors acknowledge LLM-assisted drafting. Long file (176k chars): read abstract, intro, contributions, Sec. VI results, conclusion and grep hits; did not read Secs. III-V in detail, robustness tables, case studies or appendices.

title: Deciding When Not to Decide: Indeterminacy-Aware Intrusion Detection with NeutroSENSE
evidence: Sec. III.C (closely paraphrased): the system escalates uncertain cases to the cloud or human review; Sec. IV.D sweeps the indeterminacy threshold I over 0.1-0.9.
method: NeutroSENSE: soft-voting ensemble (random forest, XGBoost, logistic regression) for IoT intrusion detection; neutrosophic truth/falsity/indeterminacy scores from class probabilities; predictions above an entropy threshold are sent to a review queue.
evaluation: IoT-CAD (Linux, 8 classes); single models as baselines. Ensemble accuracy 97% full coverage (97.31% at I<=0.9); >99.8% retained accuracy at I<=0.4; mean I 0.6223 wrong vs 0.2410 correct. No hardware or latency.
contribution: Thresholds normalised-entropy indeterminacy on an ensemble intrusion detector so uncertain IoT traffic predictions are abstained for review, raising retained accuracy above 99.8% at a reduced coverage.
flag: none of (i)-(v): classifier with a reject option applied to a domain; one-shot, per-record. Human or cloud review is asserted but never implemented or measured. No comparison with any other abstention or uncertainty method (author admits entropy and margin baselines not benchmarked), so E2 is also arguable - only comparison is the same ensemble without abstention. Class thresholds are set at the 80th percentile on the TEST set (leakage). Sample count inconsistent (text over 140,000, Table II sums to about 267,000). Edge/fog deployment claimed but no hardware or timing, so no edge cell. Coverage at I<=0.4 not stated numerically. Figures not readable in the fetch.

title: Know What You Don't Know: Selective Prediction for Early Exit DNNs
evidence: Sec. III-F (paraphrase): at each exit the deferral classifier is checked first and if hardness S_i >= beta the sample is deferred; Sec. III-B: "the expert is the one who assigns the true label".
method: SPEED: a linear deferral classifier at every early exit of a frozen BERT/RoBERTa/MobileNet flags hard samples to defer to an expert; otherwise exit on confidence or continue to next layer.
evaluation: 8 GLUE-style NLP sets, CIFAR-10, Caltech-256, OOD pairs; vs BERT-SR, SelectiveNet, Cal-RF, PBEE-SR. Avg risk/coverage 4.9/86.0 vs 6.8/85.7 (PBEE-SR); speedup 2.05x vs 1.71x. RTX 2070; no ms latency.
contribution: Adds per-exit deferral classifiers to early-exit networks so hard inputs are handed off early, cutting average selective risk from 10.6% to 4.9% at 86% coverage with 2.05x layer speedup.
flag: none of (i)-(v) cleanly: BORDERLINE (i). Deferred samples are said to go to an expert (larger model or human) but the expert is never instantiated; evaluation is pure risk-coverage plus layer-count speedup, i.e. one-shot selective prediction. Layer-wise exit is not a sequential setting in the (ii) sense. Lemma 3.1 and Theorem 3.2 give risk bounds but assume constant exit probabilities (authors call it a simplification) - not foundational enough for (v) in my reading. Eq. 4 direction (S_i < beta) contradicts the text rule (defer if S_i >= beta). Speedup is counted in layers, not wall-clock. Abstract 50% risk cut and 2.05x match Table I.

title: SAFENet: Towards a Robust Suicide Assessment in Social Media Using Selective Prediction Framework
venue: Proceedings - 2024 IEEE International Conference on Big Data, BigData 2024
evidence: "When g(x) = 0, the predictor rejects the prediction and assigns the sample to human experts." (Sec. III-A)
method: SAFENet: Longformer post features, self-adaptive training with ordinal loss, and a MaxLogit selector that abstains on low-confidence suicide-risk predictions and flags them for human review.
evaluation: Depression500 (500 Reddit users) and eRisk (170 samples); baselines Deep Gambler, SelectiveNet, CAT; F1 0.728 at 50% coverage vs 0.708 best ablation; FSR 0.786 at 85%; no latency.
contribution: SAFENet combines self-adaptive training, ordinal loss and a MaxLogit selector to abstain on low-confidence suicide-risk predictions from social media posts, improving F1 at fixed coverage over gambler and SelectiveNet baselines.
flag: none of (i)-(v) in substance: a one-shot selective classifier with a reject option applied to a domain. Borderline (i): rejected samples are said to go to a human evaluator, but no human is modelled or evaluated and rejection is a plain confidence threshold at a target coverage; maintainer may read this as (i). Inconsistencies: Table I gives SAFENet F1 0.658 at full coverage, Table II gives 0.639 (below CE at 0.649); text claims a loss at 0.60 coverage 'by a margin of 1.004%' while the table shows 0.710 vs 0.713. Tiny test sets, high variance. Did not read the qualitative analysis and conclusion closely.

title: Semi-supervised Learning to Defer Algorithm for Lung Disease Diagnosis
venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (BigData)
evidence: "The L2D algorithms will selectively direct samples to the classifier based on their conformance to the classifier's training data and defer the rest to the expert." (Sec. II-D)
method: Semi-supervised learning to defer: a feature extractor plus CoMatch-based expert predictor with a consistency regularization loss imputes missing radiologist predictions, which then train existing L2D algorithms (Mozannar, Raghu, Okati).
evaluation: NIH chest X-ray airspace opacity, one real radiologist, s=4-40 expert labels; imputed-expert accuracy 84.9-89.7% vs CoMatch 67.8-76.7%; system accuracy +1.24% (Mozannar) over CoMatch; 10GB GPU, no latency.
contribution: A consistency-regularised semi-supervised expert predictor lets learning-to-defer systems be trained when only a handful of radiologist predictions exist, raising human-AI team accuracy on chest X-ray diagnosis.
flag: (i): learning to defer to a human radiologist is the main subject. Caveats: the contribution is imputing expert labels for training, the deferral rules themselves are existing ones; single dataset, single expert, binary task; system accuracy is shown mostly in Figure 2 with gains quoted as averages in text, and no numeric system-accuracy table was seen in the extracted text. The authors' own 'Limited' ablation beats the full method at s=20 and s=40 (87.9 vs 87.6, 89.0 vs 88.6). Oddities: L2D is trained on a split called TestSet; 2D X-rays described as resampled to 224x224x224 volumetric slices. Last part of the paper (ablation table, conclusion) skimmed only.

title: From Confidence to Care: Rule-Based Escalation for Trustworthy Clinical AI
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Collaborative Advances in Software and COmputiNg (CASCON)
evidence: "A transparent Prolog policy maps <prediction, confidence, consistency, explanation> to Care-0-Care-3 via thresholds and duty-to-warn predicates, emits a human-readable trace" (Abstract; angle brackets and dash normalised to ASCII)
method: Confidence-to-Care: token log-probability summaries, semantic entropy, self-consistency and paraphrase agreement from a medical LLM feed a Prolog rule policy that assigns escalation levels Care-0 to Care-3.
evaluation: 80 QA/triage items plus synthetic red-flag cases; accuracy 74.1%, ECE 0.21 (geometric), about 35% error reduction at 80% coverage, kappa 0.62; policy inference under 2 ms; ablations only.
contribution: A two-page proposal for a Prolog rule policy that turns medical LLM confidence and consistency signals into auditable care-escalation levels, with indicative results on an 80-item question bank.
flag: none of (i)-(v) clearly; nearest is (i) since escalation implies clinician involvement, but no human is modelled. Two-page poster abstract. Table II is captioned 'ILLUSTRATIVE; REPLACE WITH FINAL', so the reported numbers are self-declared placeholders and I treat the floor as unmet; if the maintainer accepts them, the fallback is exclude-E4 (LLM abstaining on single questions). The LLM, dataset source and baseline are not named; error reduction and Care-3 rate are given only as approximate values; thresholds are admitted to be uncalibrated. Oddity: Care-0 fires on LOW confidence yet maps to the least urgent triage band. Abstract contains the typo 'Confidence-to-CCare'.

title: Risk-Aware Graph MAPPO with a Decoupled Safety Shield for Multi-Ship Collision Avoidance
venue: Proceedings - 2026 IEEE 27th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Applications, CCSSTA 2026
evidence: "The Default Safety Shield is an execution-time action correction layer. It monitors the policy action after it is generated and modifies it only when the current encounter is risky" (Sec. III-C)
method: Risk graph built from distance, DCPA and TCPA feeds a GNN actor in MAPPO (CTDE); a decoupled threshold shield blends or fully replaces the learned action at execution.
evaluation: Simplified 4-ship 2D simulator, 3 seed groups x 100 episodes; baselines rule-based controller and MAPPO-MLP plus shield ablation; CR 0.370 to 0.067, SR 0.087 to 0.220, NMR@60 0.067, ShieldStep 0.392, MinDist 97.7 m; no hardware or latency reported.
contribution: Shows that a risk-graph MAPPO actor plus a decoupled threshold shield cuts multi-ship collision rate from 0.370 to 0.067 over an unshielded MARL baseline, at some timeout cost.
flag: learned or AI system guarded: yes - MAPPO graph policy is the guarded system. Check that the shield is an empirical threshold supervisor, not a verified shield (authors state this); the rule baseline still has lower CR (0.053 vs 0.067), so the gain is over MAPPO-MLP only; abstract figures match Tables II and III; 4 ships, simplified kinematics, no AIS data, no latency or hardware; prose refers to "the present manuscript" and "SCI-style reporting", suggesting reuse of a journal draft.

title: Linear Model Predictive Safety Certification for Learning-Based Control
venue: IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC)
evidence: Sec. I: the scheme 'only filters proposed inputs that drive the system out of what we call the safe set', and Algorithm 1 otherwise applies 'the previously calculated backup controller from time k' (Sec. III).
method: Linear MPC safety certification: an online filter between a learning-based input and the plant; it admits the input only if a backup trajectory to a terminal safe set stays feasible.
evaluation: Simulation only, mass-spring-damper with 20% model error, 600 samples; qualitative baseline (unfiltered learning violates constraints in the first steps); no violation counts, no solve times, no hardware.
contribution: An MPC-based safety certification filter that admits a learning-based control input only when a backup trajectory to a robust terminal safe set remains feasible, with proved constraint satisfaction.
flag: learned or AI system guarded: yes - a generic learning-based controller u_L. Check the evaluation floor: there is NO quantitative safety metric and no ablation, the only baseline being a qualitative figure, so inclusion rests entirely on the proved guarantees (Prop. IV.1, Thm IV.2, Cor. IV.4) under the 'or a proved guarantee' clause. Single-agent; no latency measured despite the real-time claim in Sec. I; human input is mentioned only in a footnote, so no (e). Most likely overturn in this batch alongside record 5.

title: An Efficient Reachability-Based Framework for Provably Safe Autonomous Navigation in Unknown Environments
venue: IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC)
evidence: Sec. VI-A: the switching law of Eq. (10) executes the planner control inside the safe set and applies the reachability safety controller otherwise, a least restrictive filter acting 'except when the system is at the risk of violating safety'.
method: Hamilton-Jacobi reachability safety layer with warm-started and local value-function updates; a least-restrictive switching law applies the safety controller whenever the state leaves the recomputed safe set.
evaluation: Dubins-car sim plus TurtleBot 2; ablations HJI-VI vs warm-start vs local update: BRS update 45.7s vs 26.3s vs 0.6s, over-conservative states 0%-1.1%; collisions qualitative; MATLAB, i7-5820K.
contribution: A reachability-based safety layer that updates the backward reachable set online from newly sensed free space, cutting safety-computation time about 40x while overriding planner commands at the safe-set boundary.
flag: learned or AI system guarded: yes, but only partly - one nominal planner is the CNN vision-based planner of [7] (it collides with a door without the layer), the others are classical RRT and spline planners, so the learned-system condition rests on that single experiment. The quantitative results are compute time and over-conservative-state percentage; collision avoidance is shown qualitatively only, with no collision count, in both sim and the TurtleBot chair experiment. Criterion (d) is arguable: compute time is measured and real-time safe-set updating is the stated goal, but no explicit deadline or latency budget is given and compute ran on a desktop i7, so I claimed latency/jitter aware but not edge deployment. Single agent and static environments by the authors own admission; multi-agent is future work.

title: Budgeted Classification with Rejection: An Evolutionary Method with Multiple Objectives
evidence: Sec. III-A: at the final stage if max class probability is below the threshold the evaluation "is deemed inconclusive with no label assigned".
method: EMSCO: multi-objective genetic algorithm assigning features to stages of a budgeted logistic-regression cascade with confidence early exit and a final-stage reject option; optimises coverage, accepted accuracy and acquisition cost.
evaluation: Pima, Heart, Credit, two synthetic sets; vs Greedy Miser, CSTC, CO-T, CaCT LASSO. Pima accuracy/coverage/cost 71.1%/99%/242.4 vs CO-T 72%/97%/524. No inference latency; Xeon E5-2650 for ground truth.
contribution: Evolves a staged feature-acquisition classifier that exits early when confident and rejects at the last stage, reaching non-dominated accuracy, coverage and cost trade-offs on five tabular benchmarks.
flag: none of (i)-(v): BORDERLINE (ii) only nominally - feature acquisition is staged, but rejection is available only at the final stage and is not an action chosen over time; rejected inputs get no label and go nowhere (no human, no fallback). Main contribution is the evolutionary cost-sensitive search rather than the reject decision, so E1 is also defensible. Accuracy for EMSCO is over accepted inputs while GM and CSTC never reject, so Table II is not coverage-matched; CaCT LASSO beats EMSCO on accuracy on all five sets. Theorem 1 is a search-space count, not reject-option theory. No ablation of the reject option. Supplement in external repository not read.

title: AEGIS: Policy-Governed Vulnerability Management for CI/CD Software Security
venue: Annual International Computer Software and Applications Conference
evidence: "We therefore treat WARN as a deferral mechanism that routes patches into bounded human review." (Sec. I)
method: AEGIS: graph-based patch risk, MC-Dropout epistemic uncertainty and symbolic delta facts feed a deterministic policy guard choosing Block, Warn (defer to human review) or Pass for each CI/CD patch.
evaluation: Policy replay on 512-patch (5 positives) and 864-patch (47 positives) streams; baselines score-threshold, Top-K warn, uncertainty-only; matched-load false blocks 7 vs 26, loss 1.12 vs 0.39 uncertainty-only; no latency.
contribution: AEGIS gates CI/CD patches with a policy guard that blocks only when risk is high and uncertainty low and defers uncertain patches to budgeted human review, exposing trade-offs between false blocks, missed regressions and review load.
flag: (iv) primarily, also (i): a runtime gate that blocks, defers or passes patches in a stream, with deferral to human review under a review budget. Candid caveats: the full method does NOT beat the simple uncertainty-only deferral baseline on loss (Table V 1.12 vs 0.39; Table IV 0.81 vs 0.74) and the authors say so; Scenario 1 has only 5 positives; evaluation is offline policy replay on stored traces, not a live pipeline; human reviewers are a budget parameter, never studied (so no 'e'); Table VII sensitivity is directional only, no numbers; Scenario 2 (41 repair attempts, 0 unsafe) has no baseline. 'Irreversible' is used as an action class, not a time-to-irreversibility measure. Logical domain only.

title: TrafficSim: Learning to Simulate Realistic Multi-Agent Behaviors
venue: IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings - IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings
evidence: Sec. 3.2: an implicit latent variable model whose graph neural network scene interaction module over a fully connected actor graph parameterises prior, posterior and decoder, outputting a T_plan-step joint plan for all actors.
method: Implicit latent variable model over a fully connected actor graph; a GNN decoder samples a scene-level latent and rolls out joint multi-agent plans, re-planning every few simulation steps.
evaluation: ATG4D, 6500 25s snippets; baselines IDM, MTP, ESP, ILVM, AdversarialIL, DataAug; minSADE 0.57 vs 1.19-3.03, scenario collision rate 0.50% vs 1.19-11.0%; ablations M0-M3; 0.24-0.83s on GTX 1080 Ti.
contribution: A latent variable generative model over an actor interaction graph that simulates joint traffic behaviour, reaching 0.50% scenario collision rate and lower reconstruction error than motion-forecasting and imitation baselines.
flag: learned or AI system guarded: n/a - nothing is guarded. Included under (b) as latent prediction of future state over a multi-agent graph with direct predictive measures (minSFDE 1.13, minSADE 0.57) and M0-M3 ablations; RQ5 capped at 2 per the (b) rule and no prevention credited. (c) fails the primacy test: the primary claim is simulation realism, SCR is one of seven metrics, and traffic-rule violation is far worse than the IDM heuristic (2.77% vs 0.25%, ground truth 1.26%) while the text calls it 'similar'. Borderline (a) the maintainer may want to credit: the Sec. 4.2 simulation-time rejection sampling and latent gradient optimisation do discard colliding sampled plans before they are applied (SCR 0.50 to 0.33 to 0.12%, Table 5), but this is a scenario-authoring utility inside a simulator rather than interception of an acting system, so runtime_interceptor is no. The claimed 4x speedup is about 3.5x by Table 4 (0.83s to 0.24s), the runtime figure is not defined as per-tick or per-rollout, and the appendix defines SADE-SFDE with squared norms while the tables are labelled in metres.

title: Generating Useful Accident-Prone Driving Scenarios via a Learned Traffic Prior
venue: IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings - IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings
evidence: Sec. 3.1-3.2: a graph-based conditional VAE traffic prior predicting all agents future trajectories is optimised adversarially in its latent space to produce collision scenarios that stay plausible and solvable.
method: STRIVE: a graph-based CVAE traffic prior; adversarial optimisation in its latent space makes other agents collide with a fixed planner, then a solution optimisation recovers an avoidable variant.
evaluation: nuScenes, 1200 8s sequences; vs Bicycle baseline and regular scenes: collision 27.4% vs 1.2%; ADE-FDE 1.75-3.57 vs AgentFormer 1.45-2.86; ablations; planner retuning 68.6% to 54.3%; Titan RTX, 6-7min per scenario.
contribution: STRIVE generates plausible, solvable accident-prone traffic scenarios by adversarial optimisation inside a learned graph-based traffic prior, then uses them to retune a planner and cut its collision rate on challenging scenes.
flag: learned or AI system guarded: n/a at runtime - the planner adversarially attacked is rule-based, and the only online element is a learned classifier switching that planner between two hyperparameter sets from the past 2s of traffic, which adapts but cannot override or halt, so (a) fails and runtime_interceptor is no. I credited (c) because collision rate is the headline measured outcome against regular nuScenes scenes (1.2%) and the Bicycle baseline, but this is hazard GENERATION rather than hazard detection and the maintainer may read the primacy test differently. RQ5 scored 3 on the 68.6% to 54.3% challenging-scene improvement with the regular-scene rate unchanged at 4.6%; the (b) rule would cap it at 2 and that cap's stated rationale (no hazard rate exists to report) does not apply here, so please settle it. Offline only, 6-7 minutes per 10-agent scenario, no onboard or latency figures, driving domain only.

title: Curated Uncertainty Exchange: A Deployment Pattern for Trustworthy AI in Expertise-Curated Environments, Motivated by a Heritage-Viticulture Re-Analysis
venue: 2026 22nd International Conference on Distributed Computing in Smart Systems and the Internet of Things (DCOSS-IoT)
evidence: "The arbiter is a configurable rank-percentile threshold that partitions predictions into auto-commit (top 1-K) and escalate-to-expert (bottom K %)" (Sec. III-A, Pattern overview)
method: Deployment pattern (CUE): a rank-percentile confidence gate plus detection-failure abstention routes the bottom-K% of grapevine-variety predictions to an expert ampelographer; classifier left unmodified.
evaluation: None of its own: re-reads published aggregates of the vinum-Analytics pipeline (94.06% Top-1, 100% Top-5, 14.6% detection failures); Table III budget projection is illustrative, not measured; no baseline.
contribution: Position paper proposing a rank-percentile escalation gate that hands uncertain vine-variety predictions to the expert who curated the labels, with an unvalidated 15-20% review-budget hypothesis.

title: Learning to Defer to A Population with Limited Demonstrations
venue: 2025 International Conference on Digital Image Computing: Techniques and Applications (DICTA)

title: Classification with a reject option under Concept Drift: The Droplets algorithm
venue: Proceedings of the 2015 IEEE International Conference on Data Science and Advanced Analytics, DSAA 2015
evidence: "As a consequence, the algorithm is able to distinguish which observations are potentially hard to classify and can abstain from predicting in those cases" (Sec. III, Cautious stance leading to reliable predictions)

Baselines never abstain, so the comparison is Droplets on its accepted subset vs non-rejecting learners on the same subset (Table I) and on the rejected subset (Table III); no reject-capable baseline, which the authors concede as future work. title: Achievable Error Exponents for Almost Fixed-Length M-Ary Hypothesis Testing
venue: ICASSP 2023 - 2023 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)

title: The Trajectron: Probabilistic Multi-Agent Trajectory Modeling With Dynamic Spatiotemporal Graphs
venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
evidence: Method section: each agent is a node in a dynamic spatiotemporal graph and a CVAE with discrete latent z decodes a 16-component GMM over each agent's future velocities, integrated into positions.

title: A Safety-Certified Framework for Maternal Triage: Integrating Conformal Prediction and Cost-Sensitive Objective Optimization
venue: International Conference Computational Vision and Bio Inspired Computing

Doubts: abstract claims 'eliminating catastrophic false negatives' yet high-risk recall FALLS from 96.36% to 95.56% under abstention and Table IV recall is 0.9636; abstract says '100 clinically-sampled patients' but test set is N=203; coverage given as 78.30% vs 21.67% abstention (78.33%); Fig. 8 baseline 84.7% vs 85.22/85.71% in Table III; Fig. 7 at alpha=0.1 shows 22.7% non-singleton while headline uses alpha=0.05; abstract names CatBoost+LightGBM but the cost-sensitive objective is XGBoost; McNemar p=1.0000 between models. title: Semantic Consistency Drift Monitoring for Training-Free Adversarial Prompt Injection Detection in Agentic LLM Pipelines
venue: 7th International Conference on Computational Vision and Bio Inspired Computing, ICCVBIC 2026 - Proceedings
evidence: "the action plan is captured before execution. Both are passed to SCDM for a single cosine computation (<2 ms). A positive detection can trigger quarantine, human review, or pipeline rollback." (Sec. IV-D)

Check construct validity: action plans are manually written and the 40-sample corpus was built by the authors (both conceded in Sec. VIII), so there is no end-to-end injection-prevention result and no live agent; AUC 0.795 is modest, while the 5-fold CV AUC of 0.863 +/- 0.110 exceeds the headline figure; Sec. title: Adaptive Staged Medical Diagnosis From Multimodal Information: A Quality-Constrained Sequential Three-Way Classification Approach
venue: 2026 23rd International Computer Conference on Wavelet Active Media Technology and Information Processing (ICCWAMTIP)
evidence: Sec. 1: "making early diagnoses for confident patients while deferring uncertain cases for further examinations"

It is a cost-saving early-exit scheme, not a safety interceptor, and forced to decide at the last stage - maintainer may view it as closer to a cost cascade (E1). title: A Man-Machine Cooperating System Based on the Generalized Reject Model
venue: Proceedings of the International Conference on Document Analysis and Recognition, ICDAR
evidence: Abstract: "In this paper, we propose a generalized reject model that can introduce error rates after rejection."
method: Generalised reject model: confidence thresholds route each input to OCR, human+OCR double entry or human+human double entry, each with its own error rate and cost; thresholds minimise total system cost.
evaluation: Derived optimal-threshold conditions (first-order, eqs. 11-13, 16-21); synthetic normal case; 9,892 handwritten Japanese names: empirical cost minimum at T1=0.101 (single entry), T1=0.0346, T2=0.330 (double entry). No measured cost or error versus a baseline.

BORDERLINE E2: the 'proof' is a first-order optimality derivation, not a theorem with stated assumptions, and the experiments only report where the cost curve is minimised - no total cost or error rate is compared against the conventional zero-error-after-reject rule or any other baseline. title: Early Recognition of Handwritten Gestures Based on Multi-Classifier Reject Option
venue: 2017 14th IAPR International Conference on Document Analysis and Recognition (ICDAR)
evidence: Abstract: "we introduce a reject option to postpone the decision until ambiguity persists"

title: Improving the Prediction Cost of Drift Handling Algorithms by Abstaining
venue: IEEE International Conference on Data Mining Workshops, ICDMW
evidence: Abstract: "the overall prediction cost can be improved by allowing the regressor to abstain"
