flag: none of (i)-(v): one-shot hierarchical selective classification applied to network intrusion detection; analysts are named as the alarm destination but no human or hand-off is studied, and flows are scored independently. Doubts: (1) held-out "UDP Flood (18,845 samples)" is not a class in the dataset table and 18,845 is exactly the Slowloris count, while Sec. VI-A holds out Slowloris with 3,729 samples; (2) own alarm score AUROC 0.5214 on Slowloris is near chance and below Energy 0.6234 and Mahalanobis 0.6080; (3) F1 collapses from 96.50% to 32.23% under a time-ordered split, so headline numbers are upper bounds; (4) hierarchy lowers CNN1D F1 by 1.04 pp versus flat, and Table VII (97.44 at lambda 0.3) disagrees with Table V mean 96.19; AttDNN is run with consistency weight 0, i.e. without the headline loss; (5) flat+max-softmax matches selective accuracy (99.998%), the only difference is coverage (60.9% vs 94.5%); (6) the Att s123 run has n=88 coarse-only versus about 10k in other runs; (7) code-availability text mentions conformal calibration and adversarial evaluation that the paper does not report; (8) ARP Spoofing has 7 samples, none in test. Single dataset, 2-3 seeds. Novel-class alarm rate 62.1% mean, centroid family assignment 69.5%.

title: A Cost-Efficient CWE-Grounded Multi-Agent LLM Pipeline for Web and API Vulnerability Analysis: Design, Statistical Evaluation, and Implications for 5G/6G Edge Deployment
venue: IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society
evidence: "Escalation is formalized as classification with a reject option, with closed-form thresholds and proof that human review does not reduce precision." (Abstract)
method: Detector LLM proposes vulnerability findings; validator LLM scores 0-100; below 40 rejected, 70+ confirmed, 40-69 routed to a human analyst. Thresholds derived from Chow rule with fallible reviewer.
evaluation: Spiracle (10 runs, blinded two-annotator relabel) and OWASP Benchmark sample; vs CodeQL, single-agent, rule+LLM, detector-only. Precision 0.683, recall 0.867; auto-confirming escalated 0.669; 10.2% routed; 45 s per review.
contribution: A detector-validator LLM pipeline for code vulnerability triage escalates mid-confidence findings to an analyst, with cost-optimal routing thresholds derived for a fallible reviewer and a proof that review cannot lower delivered precision.
flag: (i), with a small (v) component. Borderline on MAIN contribution: this is a mixed systems paper (pipeline, reproducibility/model-drift study, benchmark evaluation); the escalation derivation is contribution 1 of 3 and opens the abstract and conclusion, but the authors state confidence-based human escalation is not novel. Maintainer may prefer exclude-E1. What is proved: Theorem 1 (expected-cost-optimal three-way threshold policy, Chow rule with reviewer accuracy alpha, band non-empty iff review cost below (2*alpha-1)c/2), Theorem 2 (precision identity for the rejecting validator), Proposition 1 (human adjudication of the band cannot lower delivered precision if alpha > 1/2); all elementary. Doubts: the deployed thresholds 40/70 were fixed first and the cost ratio is read off afterwards assuming the validator score is calibrated, which is not tested; the gain from the escalation band is small (OWASP precision 0.683 vs 0.669 with escalated auto-confirmed, vs 0.663 detector alone, FPR 0.545 vs 0.588 vs 0.604); CodeQL beats the pipeline (precision 0.782, recall 1.000, F1 0.878 vs 0.764) and the single-agent variant beats the two-agent one on every metric; escalated band posterior 0.46 (86 genuine, 101 not), rejected set 0 of 43 genuine; routing rate drifted 5.7% to 10.2% across model versions; human review cost USD 31.78-52.97 per scan dwarfs USD 0.08 inference. Text repeatedly refers to a "previous version" with corrected claims (revised manuscript). 5G/6G edge framing is discussion only, nothing measured on edge hardware. Offline code scanning, not an acting system. Long file: read abstract, contributions, Sec. III-G theory, IV-C, IV-H to IV-L partly, V, conclusion; skipped literature review, DAST results, Sec. VI-VIII deployment discussion and result tables (lost in extraction).

title: Security of AI Agents
evidence: Sec. IV.B: "A sandbox restricts the capabilities of the agent program" through local resource limits and remote whitelists, blacklists and rate limiting, and in Sec. IV.B.1 the Docker-constrained BashAgent "successfully defended against all the LLM-generated attacks".

evaluation: Preliminary experiments only: 95 AgentBench-derived security tasks where the unconstrained BashAgent executes 76 of 95 (80.0%) attacks (confidentiality 96.0%, integrity 85.7%, availability 62.9%) vs a Docker variant defending all with no figures; encryption utility 49.0% vs 47.0% (FPETS) and 85.0% vs 99.0% (FHE). No hardware or latency.

MOST LIKELY OVERTURN: it is primarily a position and taxonomy paper whose own introduction calls its experiments "preliminary", which is why I call E3, but it does propose defenses and report numbers, so the maintainer may prefer include on (a) or exclude-E4 (single agent; multi-agent appears once in Sec. III.C.1, "This strain is magnified when multiple agents operate concurrently", and is never evaluated). Also: the defended variant has no quantitative result beyond "defended against all the LLM-generated attacks", there is no baseline beyond the two variants and no ablation, Definitions 4.1-4.2 are stated with no theorems or proofs, the session-management and session-aware-model defenses are unimplemented, and there is no latency or human-handoff content.

title: Analyzing Agent Collisions in AI-Aided Energy Management Systems
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Communications, Control, and Computing Technologies for Smart Grids, SmartGridComm 2025 - Proceedings
evidence: "We define an operational collision as any time step t during which one or more network constraints are violated as a direct result of agents' uncoordinated decisions" (Sec. IV-A, Definition of Operational Collision)
method: Partially observable Markov game over networked microgrids with PPO agents; a monitoring module logs voltage and thermal violations per time step, aggregates per-agent severity metrics and attributes collisions to policies.
evaluation: IEEE 34-bus feeder with three IEEE 13-bus microgrids in PandaPower, PPO with two-layer GRU policies, 2,628,000 steps, 2018-2019 train and 2020 test; collision frequency 0.568 independent vs 0.285 shared reward; MG2 holds 78.4% of violations.

flag: learned or AI system guarded: yes - the analysed agents are PPO MARL microgrid controllers. Detection is logging and post-hoc attribution, never an override, so (a) fails and (c) carries the record. Internal inconsistency the maintainer should check: the text claims shared rewards left collisions 'rare' and 'nearly eliminated', yet Table I gives a 0.285 mean violation frequency over the final 100 years and Table II shows MG1 and MG3 totals HIGHER under shared reward (50,020.55 vs 41,228.27 and 80,406.57 vs 58,575.85). Training is reported as 8,760 x 300 steps but figures are axis-labelled in 300 years. Figures 2 and 3 carry no absolute numbers, and the only contrast is independent vs shared reward with no external baseline.

title: Cognitive-State-Driven LLM Decision Agent for Fault Diagnosis of Rotating Machinery Under Incomplete Evidence
venue: 2026 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety Engineering (SRSE)
evidence: "Both actions prevent automatic submission, but REQUEST_EXPERT further transfers the case to human review." (Sec. II-E)
method: LoRA-tuned Qwen2.5-14B reads a cognitive-state prompt (judge probabilities, uncertainty, OOD, case-memory signals) and chooses SUBMIT, MORE_WINDOWS, ABSTAIN or REQUEST_EXPERT; SFT on a rule policy, then GRPO.
evaluation: PU bearing data, 4,018 decision states; GRPO vs SFT v1/v1.1. Premature submits 181 to 119; wrong auto-diagnosis 4.16% to 3.56%; SUBMIT coverage 0.323 to 0.294; two A100 GPUs, no latency.

flag: (i) and nominally (ii). Weak evidence, maintainer should check: (1) the authors state results are "development analyses" because the same 4,018 records are used for checkpoint selection and evaluation, no independent test set; (2) records from the held-out bearings were used to fit OOD detectors, build case memory and train the LLM policy (leakage, acknowledged); (3) the sequential framing is not evaluated: each decision state is scored independently, no complete episodes, no final diagnostic accuracy; (4) most metrics are agreement with the hand-written rule policy the model imitates, and that rule policy itself, or a plain confidence threshold, is not reported as a baseline on true-label metrics, so it is unclear the LLM adds anything over the rules; only wrong-diagnosis rate and SUBMIT selective accuracy (0.8713 to 0.8788) use true labels; (5) the gain comes with lower coverage and more conservative MORE_WINDOWS (449 to 507), agreement change not significant (+0.0025, CI spans 0); (6) no human in any experiment, expert review is only an action label, so (e) not credited and human handoff gap cell not claimed; (7) single dataset, single seed 42, 32B model no better than 14B. A 14B LLM as gate has no latency figures. Short conference paper (SRSE 2026).

title: A General Safety Framework for Learning-Based Control in Uncertain Robotic Systems
evidence: Abstract: a "least-restrictive, safety-preserving control law that intervenes only when the computed safety guarantees require it"; the switching law Eq. 8 (Sec. III-A) applies the learned action when V(x) is positive and the safe action otherwise.
method: Hamilton-Jacobi reachability safety filter with Gaussian-process disturbance learning; a least-restrictive switch hands control from an arbitrary learning-based controller to a safe policy when the value function or safety confidence drops.
evaluation: Quadrotor flight tests (Pelican, Hummingbird, VICON, STARMAC) with a with-validation vs without-validation ablation; outcomes qualitative - learning from free fall without ever crashing, and without validation the vehicle violates constraints and repeatedly strikes the ground; safe-set recompute about 2 s, lookup tables constant time, MATLAB on an offboard laptop over ROS.
contribution: A modular least-restrictive safety framework that uses reachability analysis and Gaussian-process disturbance learning to override a learning-based controller only when its guarantees require it.
flag: learned or AI system guarded: yes - a policy-gradient RL quadrotor controller (linear feedback weights), guarded without modifying the learner. Check the evaluation floor: the hardware experiments quantify no collision, violation or intervention counts, giving only qualitative outcomes plus the with/without-validation ablation, so inclusion rests on the formal results (Props. 1-7, Cors. 1-2, robust controlled invariance, probabilistic Lyapunov-rate bound); the global criterion is only approximated (Eq. 18 uses an approximation, numerics reach about 25 dimensions, and the local result is called "a useful heuristic effort"); single agent, so (c) does not hold and "Multi-Agent" appears only in the testbed name; compute is offboard MATLAB with no real-time budget, so (d) does not hold; human handoff is only a remark that "pilot handoffs, for instance, are notoriously prone to result in accidents".

title: Probabilistic Model Predictive Safety Certification for Learning-Based Control
evidence: Introduction: the proposed input is either "certified as safe and is applied, or it is overwritten by the previous safe backup controller", and Sec. III.B implements "a minimal safe modification" whenever safety cannot be verified.
method: Probabilistic model predictive safety certification: an MPC safety filter picking the nominal input closest to the learner's proposal subject to a chance-constrained safe backup trajectory, overwriting the proposal otherwise.
evaluation: Simulation only (nonlinear car, 0.1 s sampling, horizon 30, 98% probability from 30 s of data, 30 episodes shown and 100 experiments); baseline is the uncertified learner; violations and interventions reported qualitatively (safe in every episode, interventions fall after about 30 episodes, slightly slower convergence); offline tightening in YALMIP-MOSEK, no online solver or timing.
contribution: A probabilistic model predictive safety certification filter that minimally modifies a reinforcement learner's input so a chance-constrained safe backup trajectory always remains available.
flag: learned or AI system guarded: yes - a Bayesian-optimization policy search learning a linear control law, filtered at runtime. Check the evaluation floor: no violation counts, intervention counts or reward values are given, only figures and the claim that the framework "enables safe learning in every episode", so inclusion rests on Theorem IV.5 plus recursive feasibility; the guarantee is probabilistic at level p_theta and leans on Assumptions IV.3-IV.4 and the "practical assumption" V.1; the final tightened velocity bound 19.97 m/s is reported as looser than the original 19.8 m/s, which looks inconsistent; single agent and no solver, hardware or latency figures (the authors only cite "real-time capable" solvers), so (c) and (d) do not hold; human input is mentioned only in a footnote.

title: Cooperative Resilience in Artificial Intelligence Multiagent Systems
evidence: Abstract: the paper is "proposing a clear definition of 'cooperative resilience' and outlining a methodology for its quantitative measurement"; disruptions are injected into the environment and no mechanism screens or overrides agent actions (Sec. 3).

evaluation: Melting Pot 2.0 Commons Harvest Open; 9 apple-removal scenarios and 3 unsustainable-bot scenarios; the only comparison is RL vs LLM agents; no numeric resilience scores in the text (heatmaps and five-episode curves only); no baseline controller, no ablation, no hardware or latency.

flag: learned or AI system guarded: yes for the agents (PPO policies and GPT-4 agents) but nothing guards them - there is no runtime override, veto, halt or deferral anywhere, so (a) fails, and (c) fails the primacy test because the primary claim and primary outcome are a resilience score from deviations between performance and reference curves, not a hazard, collision, violation or detection rate against a baseline or ablation. title: A Confidence-Aware Human–Machine Collaboration Framework for Harmful Meme Detection
venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems
evidence: "introducing a deferral strategy that delegates low-confidence samples to human experts while leveraging proxy labeling and a fusion model to refine decision quality" (Abstract)

evaluation: Five meme datasets, ExplainHM/IntMeme/LLaVA; vs no-deferral baseline over thresholds 0.70-0.98 and simulated human accuracy 0.75-1.0. Macro-F1 gains 0.05-4.5 points at earliest improving setting; 2-68% deferred; 10-16 s overhead, RTX 4090.

Maintainer may prefer exclude-E4. Figures with the main curves not readable from text.

title: FCD: Fallback Cognitive Deferral in Complex Human–Machine Collaboration Tasks

Doubts: one-shot classification only, no sequential, multi-agent or latency aspect; the 'RL' switch is a one-step actor-critic on i.i.d. samples.
